items.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 21 at 4:10AM EDT until September 22 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
items.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Delaware and New Jersey coasts.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
items.instruction:
Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you. Don't go into the water
at unguarded beaches. If caught in a rip current, relax and float
and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel to
the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

items.headline: Gale Watch issued September 21 at 6:08AM EDT until September 24 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, northeast winds 20 to 30
kt and seas 6 to 9 ft expected. For the Gale Watch, northeast
winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt and seas 8 to 13 ft
possible.

* WHERE...Atlantic coastal waters of New Jersey and Delaware out
to 20 NM.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, from 11 AM this morning
to 6 PM EDT Tuesday. For the Gale Watch, from Tuesday evening
through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds can cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Gale conditions may continue into Friday.
items.instruction:
Mariners should consider altering plans to avoid possible
hazardous conditions.  Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter
course, and/or secure the vessel for severe wind and seas.
